claims.head: Strength vs. Strength
claims.body: The Devils are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Senators are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Senators.
claims.nums: New Jersey 6th for the power play (8.3 expected goals per 60) · Ottawa 5th for the penalty kill

Ottawa: 7.0 expected goals allowed per 60 shorthanded, 5th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 4 and 5 games this season.

claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Senators are near the top at keeping shots away. Hot take: the Devils break through anyway.
claims.call: The Devils’ shot volume score is above 100, the league average, against the Senators.

claims.head: Bruisers vs. Finesse
claims.body: The Senators hit a lot, but the Devils mostly don’t. Ottawa is near the top of the league for physicality, and New Jersey is one of the worst. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Senators.

NJD.head: The Devils have a lot going for them
NJD.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. New Jersey has home-ice advantage. The Senators can make it interesting if they get good looks.

OTT.head: A tough matchup for the Senators
OTT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. New Jersey has home-ice advantage. The Senators can pull it off if they get good looks.

story.head: Strength vs. Strength
paras: The Devils are 2-2-0. The Senators have won two in a row.

items.text: The Senators are newly without William Eklund, and have had to make do without Jake Sanderson all season.
The Devils have been without Connor Brown all season.
Nico Hischier is two goals from passing Travis Zajac for third on the Devils’ all-time goals list.
Linus Ullmark is 6-1-0 in New Jersey in his career.
